rules.title: Prohibition on Sale of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms in Berkeley
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.key_value: prohibition on sale of coordinated pricing algorithms

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to any person or entity selling, licensing, or providing coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords

rules.exemptions: Does not include: (a) products that publish aggregated/anonymous rental data without recommending prices; (b) products for establishing affordable housing rent/income limits; (c) products for market research, appraisals, or software development/testing
rules.interaction: Works in conjunction with subsection B to create comprehensive prohibition on both supply and use of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Prohibition on Landlord Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms in Berkeley
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. Each separate month and each separate unit constitutes a distinct violation.
rules.key_value: prohibition on landlord use of coordinated pricing algorithms

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to all landlords setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as subsection A: aggregated data reports, affordable housing compliance tools, market research/appraisal tools, software development/testing
rules.interaction: Coordinated pricing algorithm defined in § 13.63.020(A) as using Competitor Data (non-public data less than 90 days old) to recommend rents/occupancy in coordination between landlords
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley. Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each 
separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the coordinated pricing 
algorithm, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.

rules.title: Maximum Tenant Screening Fee for 2026
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a maximum tenant screening fee of $68.96 for 2026. Landlords must provide tenants with a copy of their credit report within 7 days, a receipt for the fee, an itemized list of expenses and time spent, and a refund of any unused portion.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to residential rental properties in Berkeley

rules.interaction: Implements state law California Civil Code Section 1950.6 at local level
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code 13.78; California Civil Code Section 1950.6
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96
Landlords may use screening fees to obtain information about a prospective tenant like a consumer credit report. Prospective tenants should expect to receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of receipt by the landlord, a receipt for the fee paid and an itemized list of any out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord on the screening, and a refund of any unused portion of the fee.

rules.title: Requirement to Use Reusable Screening Report
rules.requirement: If a prospective tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it and cannot charge a separate screening fee for obtaining the same information.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies when prospective tenant provides a reusable screening report

rules.interaction: Prevents duplicate screening fees when tenant already has report
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code 13.78; California Civil Code Section 1950.6
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

rules.title: Prohibition on Screening Fees When No Unit Available
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available. Landlords must also return screening fees to applicants not selected or have a policy to review applications in order received and not charge fees to applicants not considered.
rules.key_value: no fee when no unit available; refund or first-come policy required

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to all tenant screening situations

rules.interaction: Prevents landlords from collecting fees when unit is unavailable or from applicants who will not be considered
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code 13.78; California Civil Code Section 1950.6
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available. The landlord must also return a screening fee to any applicant not selected, or have a policy under which they: (1) review applications in the order received and the first qualified applicant gets the unit, and (2) do not charge a screening fee to any applicant not considered.

rules.title: Applicability to Existing Rental Agreements
rules.requirement: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of any contractual language in any rental agreement or lease to the contrary. Any provision of an existing rental agreement or lease that violates the provisions of this chapter are unenforceable.
rules.key_value: applies to all agreements; conflicting provisions unenforceable

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to all residential rental agreements in Berkeley

overrides: Any conflicting provisions in existing rental agreements or leases
rules.interaction: Ensures screening fee protections cannot be waived by contract
rules.quoted_span: Chapter 13.78 applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of any contractual language in any rental agreement or lease to the contrary. Any provision of an existing rental agreement or lease that violates the provisions of this chapter are unenforceable.

rules.title: Service Member Security Deposit Protection
rules.requirement: A landlord shall not demand or receive security exceeding one month's rent from a service member, and shall not refuse to rent to a service member because the landlord cannot charge more than one month's rent as security.

coverage_conditions.text: Prospective tenant is a service member as defined in Military and Veterans Code § 400

rules.exemptions: None
rules.interaction: Overrides the two-month exception for small landlords when tenant is service member
rules.quoted_span: Subparagraph (A) shall not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member. A landlord shall not refuse to enter into a rental agreement for residential property with a prospective tenant who is a service member because this subparagraph prohibits the landlord from demanding or receiving a greater amount of security than that which is established in paragraph (1).

rules.title: Service Member Higher Security Disclosure and Return
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member higher than standard security due to credit history or other factors, the landlord must provide written statement of the amount and explanation, and must return the additional amount after six months if tenant is not in arrears.

coverage_conditions.text: Service member charged higher security due to credit/housing history or other tenant-related factor

rules.exemptions: None
rules.interaction: Applies when service member is charged higher security within the one-month limit
rules.quoted_span:
On or after April 1, 2025, if a landlord or its agent charges a service member who rents residential property in which the service member will reside a higher than standard or advertised security pursuant to paragraph (1) due to the credit history, credit score, housing history, or other factor related to the tenant, the landlord shall provide the tenant with a written statement, on or before the date the lease is signed, of the amount of the higher security and an explanation why the higher security amount is being charged. The additional amount of security shall be returned to the tenant after no more than six months of residency if the tenant
is not in arrears for any rent due during that period.

rules.title: Security Deposit Return Timeline and Itemized Statement
rules.requirement: No later than 21 calendar days after tenant vacates, landlord must furnish itemized statement of security disposition and return any remaining portion. Statement must include basis and amount of deductions, with supporting documentation including photographs, bills, invoices, or receipts for charges over $125.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to all residential tenancies

the expiration of a fixed-term lease, the landlord shall furnish the tenant, a copy of an itemized statement indicating the basis for, and the amount of, any security received and the disposition of the security, and shall return any remaining portion of the security to the tenant

rules.title: Electronic Security Deposit Return Requirement
rules.requirement: If landlord received security or rental payments electronically, landlord must return remaining security electronically to bank account or financial institution designated by tenant in writing, or by electronic/virtual method agreed to in writing, unless parties agree to another method in writing.

rules.exemptions: Parties may agree in writing to alternative return method

rules.quoted_span:
If the landlord received the security or rental payments from the tenant electronically, the landlord shall return the remainder of the security electronically to a bank account or other financial
institution designated by the tenant in writing, or by any electronic or virtual method available to the landlord if agreed to in writing by the tenant. Alternatively, the landlord and tenant may, by written agreement, designate another method of return

rules.title: General prohibition on rent control in Massachusetts
rules.requirement: No city or town in Massachusetts may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except under very limited voluntary conditions. Any rent control regulation must be entirely voluntary after six months and property owners can opt out without consequence.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to all cities and towns in Massachusetts

rules.exemptions: Cities/towns may adopt voluntary rent control under specific conditions outlined in subsections (a), (b), and (c)
rules.interaction: This state law preempts any local rent control ordinances that do not meet the voluntary compliance requirements
rules.quoted_span:
No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
(a) after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced, and the property of a person or entity declining to have his or its property subjected to such regulation shall be wholly unaffected by any aspect of the rent control regulation

rules.title: Exemptions from voluntary rent control - small landlords and higher-rent units
rules.requirement: Any voluntary rent control regulation may not apply to rental units owned by persons or entities owning fewer than ten rental units, or to units with fair market rent exceeding $400.

rules.exemptions: Units owned by landlords with fewer than 10 units; units with fair market rent over $400
rules.interaction: Limits scope of any permissible voluntary rent control regulation
rules.quoted_span: such regulation may not include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from such regulation, nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400

rules.title: Prohibition on eviction regulation in voluntary rent control
rules.requirement: Any voluntary rent control regulation adopted by a city or town may not include regulation of evictions.

rules.title: New Jersey Residential Rental Application Fee Cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes which exceeds $50. This amount is adjusted annually based on the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, New York-Northern New Jersey-Long Island Metropolitan Area.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to residential rental properties for dwelling purposes in New Jersey

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to: (1) a dwelling unit located in a one-family or two-family dwelling that is offered for rent; or (2) a licensee of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission, unless the licensee is the landlord of the residential rental property
rules.interaction: Violations subject to penalties of up to $500 for first offense, up to $750 for second offense, and up to $1,000 for each subsequent offense. Amount wrongfully charged shall be remitted to the applicant or prospective tenant.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

rules.title: San Francisco Just Cause Eviction Requirement
rules.requirement: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a 'just cause' reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. The mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute 'just cause' for eviction.

rules.interaction: Works in conjunction with 17 enumerated just cause reasons under Section 37.9(a)
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance

rules.quoted_span: Failure to cure a substantial breach of a rental agreement or lease;

rules.title: Nuisance as Just Cause

rules.title: Notice to Quit for Nonpayment of Rent
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent, landlords must provide fourteen days' written notice to quit to terminate an estate at will tenancy. Tenants who have not received a similar notice within the prior twelve months may prevent termination by paying or tendering full rent due within ten days of receiving the notice.
rules.key_value: 14 days notice; 10 days to cure if no prior notice in 12 months

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to estate at will tenancies where tenant has neglected or refused to pay rent

rules.exemptions: Cure right does not apply if tenant received similar notice within prior 12 months
rules.interaction: This provision creates a shorter notice period than the general 3-month requirement for estate at will terminations, but includes tenant cure rights
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.

rules.title: Required Notification in Nonpayment Notice to Quit
rules.requirement: Every notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must contain specific notification informing tenants of their right to prevent termination by paying full rent due within ten days if they have not received a similar notice within the last twelve months. Failure to include this notification extends the tenant's cure period until the answer is due in any eviction action.
rules.key_value: Mandatory tenant notification language; failure extends cure period

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to all notices to quit for nonpayment of rent in estate at will tenancies

rules.exemptions: None specified
rules.interaction: Failure to include required notification does not invalidate the notice but extends tenant cure rights
rules.quoted_span: Every notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent shall contain the following notification to the tenant: ''If you have not received a notice to quit for nonpayment of rent within the last twelve months, you have a right to prevent termination of your tenancy by paying or tendering to your landlord, your landlord's attorney or the person to whom you customarily pay your rent the full amount of rent due within ten days after your receipt of this notice.'' If any notice to determine an estate at will for nonpayment of rent shall fail to contain such notification, the time within which the tenant receiving the notice would be entitled to pay or tender rent pursuant to this section shall be extended to the day the answer is due in any action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises.

the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board

rules.title: Just Cause Eviction Requirement After 12 Months Occupancy

rules.title: Prohibition on Source of Income Discrimination in Housing
rules.requirement: Housing owners cannot discriminate against tenants based on their lawful source of income, including federal housing vouchers and public assistance. Inquiries about income level or source are permitted, but denial based on source of income is unlawful.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to all housing accommodations in California

rules.exemptions: Making written or oral inquiry concerning level or source of income is not discrimination

rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.

rules.title: Notice Period to Terminate Estate at Will Tenancy
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide three months' written notice to terminate an estate at will tenancy, or notice equal to the interval between rent payment periods or thirty days (whichever is longer) if rent is payable at periods less than three months.
rules.key_value: 3 months or interval between rent payments or 30 days, whichever is longer

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to estate at will tenancies in Massachusetts

rules.exemptions: Shorter notice period applies for nonpayment of rent cases (14 days)
rules.interaction: This general notice requirement is superseded by the 14-day notice provision for nonpayment of rent cases

rules.title: Anti-Retaliation Protection for Tenant Reporting and Organizing
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from taking reprisals against tenants for reporting code violations, exercising legal rights, or organizing tenant unions. Tenants who experience retaliation are entitled to damages of one to three months' rent or actual damages (whichever is greater), plus costs and attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: Damages: 1-3 months rent or actual damages (whichever greater) plus costs and attorney fees

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to residential premises tenants who engage in protected activities including reporting violations, exercising legal rights, or organizing tenant unions

rules.exemptions: None specified
rules.interaction: Creates rebuttable presumption of retaliation if termination notice (except for nonpayment), rent increase, or substantial alteration of tenancy terms occurs within 6 months of protected activity
rules.quoted_span: Any person or agent thereof who threatens to or takes reprisals against any tenant of residential premises for the tenant's act of, commencing, proceeding with, or obtaining relief in any judicial or administrative action the purpose of which action is to obtain damages under, or otherwise enforce, any federal, state or local law, regulation, by-law or ordinance, which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or exercising the tenant's rights pursuant to section one hundred and twenty-four D of chapter one hundred and sixty-four; or reporting to the board of health or, in the city of Boston to the commissioner of housing inspection or to any other board having as its objective the regulation of residential premises a violation or a suspected violation of any health or building code or of any other municipal by-law or ordinance, or state or federal law or regulation which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or reporting or complaining of such violation or suspected violation in writing to the landlord or to the agent of the landlord; or for organizing or joining a tenants' union or similar organization, or for making or expressing an intention to make, a payment of rent to an organization of unit owners pursuant to paragraph (c) of section six of chapter one hundred and eighty-three A shall be liable for damages which shall not be less than one month's rent or more than three month's rent, or the actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, and the costs of the suit, including a reasonable attorney's fee.

rules.title: Broker Fee Payment Restriction - Effective August 1, 2025
rules.requirement: Any fee charged by a licensed broker or salesperson for finding rental residential real property shall only be paid by the party (lessor or tenant) who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson. A broker may only contract with either the prospective tenant or the landlord, not both parties.
rules.key_value: Fee paid only by contracting party

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to licensed brokers and salespersons finding rental residential real property in Massachusetts

rules.exemptions: None specified
rules.interaction: Amends prior version of Section 87DDD 1/2 which did not restrict who could pay broker fees

Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Individualized Assessment Required for Criminal Record Denials
rules.requirement: Housing providers may only withdraw a conditional offer based on criminal record if they determine by preponderance of evidence that withdrawal is necessary for a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest. They must conduct an individualized assessment considering six specific factors including nature/severity of offense, applicant's age at time of offense, time elapsed, rehabilitation evidence, safety impact, and connection to rental property.

coverage_conditions.text: Required when withdrawing conditional offer based on criminal record

rules.exemptions: None specified
rules.interaction: Applicant has right to appeal and provide evidence within process
rules.quoted_span:
A housing provider may withdraw a
conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if the housing
provider determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that the withdrawal is
necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
(2)   If a housing provider withdraws a conditional
offer, the housing provider shall provide the applicant with written
notification that includes, with specificity, the reason or reasons for the
withdrawal of the conditional offer and an opportunity to appeal the denial by
providing evidence to the housing provider demonstrating inaccuracies within
the applicant's criminal record or evidence of rehabilitation or other
mitigating factors.
(3)   The housing provider shall perform an
individualized assessment of the application in light of the following factors:
(a)   the nature and severity of the criminal offense;
(b)   the age of the applicant at the time of the
occurrence of the criminal offense;
(c)   the time which has elapsed since the occurrence
of the criminal offense;
(d)   any information produced by the applicant, or
produced on the applicant's behalf, in regard to the applicant's rehabilitation
and good conduct since the occurrence of the criminal offense;
(e)   the degree to which the criminal offense, if it
reoccurred, would negatively impact the safety of the housing provider's other
tenants or property; and
(f)   whether the criminal offense occurred on or was
connected to property that was rented or leased by the applicant.

rules.title: Good Cause Eviction Requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant and must be able to prove in court that grounds for eviction exist. No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease without good cause.

rules.title: Warrant for Possession Timing Requirements
rules.requirement: A warrant for possession may not be issued until three business days after the judgment for possession is granted. The tenant has three business days to move after the warrant is served. A landlord must apply for a warrant for possession within 30 days from the date of the judgment for possession unless the judgment is vacated.

The warrant for possession may not be issued unt il three (3) business 
days after the judgment for possession is granted. The tenant has three (3) business days to move 
all persons and belongings from the premises. If the tenant does not move after three (3) business 
days from the time the warrant for possession was served on the tenant, the landlord may arrange 
for the Court Officer to have the tenant evicted or locked out (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-57).

rules.title: At-Fault Just Cause Grounds for Eviction
rules.requirement: At-fault just cause includes: default in rent payment; breach of material lease term; maintaining/committing nuisance; committing waste; refusal to renew lease after written request; criminal activity on property or directed at owner/agent; unauthorized assignment/subletting; refusal to allow lawful entry; unlawful use of premises; employee/agent failure to vacate after termination; failure to deliver possession after notice to terminate.

rules.title: Income Standard for Government Rent Subsidy Recipients Must Be Based on Tenant Portion

(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.

rules.title: Rebuttable Presumption of Retaliation for Termination or Rent Increase Within Six Months
rules.requirement: A termination notice (except for nonpayment of rent), rent increase, or substantial alteration of tenancy terms within six months after a tenant engages in protected activities creates a rebuttable presumption of retaliation. The landlord must rebut this with clear and convincing evidence of independent justification.
rules.key_value: 6-month presumption period; clear and convincing evidence standard required to rebut

coverage_conditions.text: Applies when termination notice (except nonpayment), rent increase, or substantial tenancy alteration occurs within 6 months of protected tenant activity

rules.exemptions: Termination notices for nonpayment of rent are excluded from the presumption
rules.interaction: Works in conjunction with the anti-retaliation damages provision in the same statute
rules.quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities. Such presumption shall be rebutted only by clear and convincing evidence that such person's action was not a reprisal against the tenant and that such person had sufficient independent justification for taking such action, and would have in fact taken such action, in the same manner and at the same time the action was taken, regardless of tenants engaging in, or the belief that tenants had engaged in, activities protected under this section.

for
drug-related criminal activity for the
manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally
assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime
registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.

rules.title: Eviction for Failure to Pay Rent - Notice Requirements

If a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord may immediately take legal action to have the 
tenant evicted. The landlord is not required to give the tenant notice before filing an 
eviction suit, except if the tenant resides in federally subsidized housing. I f the tenant 
resides in federally subsidized housing a 14-day notice must be given before filing a suite 
for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(a)).

15 days from the date of the notice.

disorderly conduct and that conduct destroys the peace and quiet of the other tenants living 
in the building or neighborhood, the landlord may file a suite for eviction. A Notice to Quit 
must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A.
